We need to ensure no cycle of length <7.

Any cycle must include at least one cross edge, because the tree is acyclic. Actually a cycle could include multiple cross edges.

Case 1: Cycle contains exactly one cross edge. Then the rest of the cycle is the unique tree path between its endpoints. The tree distance between any two level-3 vertices in different branches is 6. So cycle length = 1 + 6 = 7. Good. Between same branch, no cross edges. So exactly one cross edge gives girth 7.

Case 2: Cycle contains exactly two cross edges. Let the cross edges be e1 = u-v and e2 = w-x. The cycle consists of e1, e2, and tree paths connecting v to w and x to u (or some combination). Since the graph is basically a tree plus edges at the leaves, the cycle will traverse from u to v via e1, then from v to w via tree path, then e2 from w to x, then tree path from x back to u. The total length = 2 + dist_tree(v,w) + dist_tree(x,u). Note that u,w,x,v are level-3 vertices. The tree paths go up to root.
